findings.issue: Comparison inverted: 工場より marks the factory as the standard of comparison ('better THAN the factory'), but the literal translation states the factory itself is better. lit_pt ('Que a fábrica, muito mais bom') has it right; lit_en teaches the opposite meaning of より.
findings.current: The factory is much better, you know.
findings.suggested: Than the factory, (it's) much better, you know.

findings.issue: Meaning inverted: めったにない = 'hardly ever happens/exists', but 'it rarely fails to happen' means it almost always happens. The literal translation asserts the opposite of the Japanese (and of en/pt/expl).
findings.current: As for a good chance coming twice, it rarely fails to happen.
findings.suggested: As for a good chance coming twice, it hardly ever happens.

findings.issue: Meaning inverted: 'raramente não existe' = 'rarely fails to exist' = almost always exists. めったにない means 'quase nunca existe/acontece'. Stacking 'raramente' + 'não existe' double-negates and reverses the sense.
findings.current: Quanto à coisa de a boa ocasião vir duas vezes, raramente não existe.
findings.suggested: Quanto à coisa de a boa ocasião vir duas vezes, quase nunca existe.

findings.issue: The literal rendering turns a genuine question into a second-person tag assertion: か here is a real interrogative ('do I have to go?', as en/pt/expl all state), not a confirmation tag 'right?', and the implied subject is the speaker, not 'you'.
findings.current: You have to go (= it won't do otherwise), right?
findings.suggested: If (I) don't go, it won't do — ? (= do I have to go?)

findings.issue: Same distortion as lit_en: 'né?' renders the interrogative か as a confirmation tag, turning the speaker's real question ('Eu preciso ir?') into an assertion seeking agreement; 'não fica' is also an odd rendering of なりません next to the correct 'não dá'.
findings.current: Se não for, não fica (= não dá), né?
findings.suggested: Se (eu) não for, não vai dar — ? (= preciso ir?)

findings.issue: 行けない is the negative potential ('cannot go'), taught explicitly in the tokens and rendered in lit_en ('Since I couldn't go'). 'Instead of going myself' drops the inability and suggests a free choice not in the Japanese.
findings.current: Instead of going myself, I sent a gift.
findings.suggested: Since I couldn't go, I sent a gift instead.

findings.issue: Same loss as en: 'Em vez de ir' omits the potencial negativo 行けない ('não poder ir') that the tokens and lit_pt teach, implying escolha em vez de impossibilidade.
findings.current: Em vez de ir [eu mesmo], mandei um presente.
findings.suggested: Como não podia ir, mandei um presente no lugar.

findings.issue: The intensifier ずっと — the pedagogical target of this sentence per expl_en — is dropped: 'better' instead of 'much/far better'. pt correctly has 'bem melhor'.
findings.current: That will be better than the factory.
findings.suggested: That will be much better than the factory.

findings.issue: 'brinde' means a promotional freebie (or a toast) in pt-BR and does not fit 贈り物 in this context of a personal gift sent in one's place; 'presente' alone is the contextual gloss.
